newsitem.title: GERMANY: German winter rape plantings seen nine pct higher.
newsitem.headline: German winter rape plantings seen nine pct higher.

text.p: German winter rapeseed plantings in the 1996/97 season were seen rising nine percent from last year to 850,000 hectares, grain trader Toepfer said in its monthly market report on Wednesday.
Toepfer said the estimate was preliminary and had been obtained from the Union for the Promotion of Oil and Protein Crops (Ufop), which based them on a private farmers survey.
The total included plantings of industrial seed for non-food use on an estimated 120,000 ha compared with 240,000 ha last year.
Toepfer noted some 13 percent of last year's winter rapeseed crop had suffered damage from a harsh winter and the affected areas had to be resown to rape and other crops in the spring.
Weather conditions were beneficial for the time being, and soils benfitted from heavy rainfall in October and November.
Spring rapeseed plantings in 96/97 may be around 40,000-50,000 ha compared with 75,890 ha in 95/96, Toepfer said separately. --Vera Eckert, Hamburg newsroom, +49-40-41903275
